data.name: Shantinath
data.gender_notes: Shantinath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shantinath is the name of the 16th Jain Tirthankara, known for his teachings of peace and non-violence. The name Shantinath carries the meaning “Peaceful Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shantinath usually hope their child will grow to embody peaceful lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who embodies inner peace and tranquility.
data.etymology: Shantinath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Peaceful Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shantinath total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Shantinath is a revered figure in Jainism, an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes non-violence, self-control, and detachment. The name "Shantinath" carries a deep cultural significance, as it represents the peace and tranquility that one can achieve through spiritual growth and disciplined living. Jain monasteries, temples, and artwork dedicated to Shantinath are prevalent throughout India and Nepal, reflecting the deep influence and importance of this figure in the region's cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Shantinath is believed to have attained liberation (Nirvana) through immense spiritual practices and self-discipline. His teachings of peace, ahimsa (non-violence), and compassion continue to inspire and guide Jain practitioners worldwide. The name "Shantinath" is a reminder that inner peace and tranquility can be attained through spiritual growth, and that one should strive to live a life free from violence and harm to others. In this way, the name carries a profound spiritual significance, embodying the ideal of personal transformation and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shantinath, meaning 'Lord of Peace', embodies the serene and tranquil aspect of Tirthankara Mahavira. He symbolizes inner peace, harmony, and the elimination of suffering through self-control and enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas, Upanishads, or other scriptures

historical_references.reference: Shantinath is considered the 16th Tirthankara in Jainism and is also known as Lord Shanti or Lord Peace. He is believed to have lived around 800 BC in the present-day Rajasthan region of India.
historical_references.context: Jainism, 16th Tirthankara, Lord Shanti, Rajasthan region, India

historical_references.reference: Shantinath is also revered in Buddhism as a Bodhisattva named Avalokitesvara or Chenrezik. In Buddhist texts, he is described as the embodiment of compassion and is believed to help those who seek relief from suffering.
historical_references.time_period: Later centuries, starting from around the 2nd century AD

modern_usage.modern_context: Shantinath is a revered figure in Jainism, known for his teachings of peace and compassion. He is one of the 24 Tirthankaras and is celebrated on Mahavir Jayanti, a major Jain festival. In modern times, Shantinath is a popular figure on social media platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and Reddit, where devotees share images, quotes, and stories related to his life and teachings. The trends of spirituality and Jainism continue to grow, making Shantinath a relevant and inspiring figure for many.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Shantinath, a teacher in Kathmandu, Nepal, shares that their name Shantinath meaning "Peaceful Lord" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
